scope: Real installed reader supervisor and child, unchanged production image/entrypoint/grants. One stopped child and one successor session, without scientific input or inference; local signed API, no live model.

reader.original_grants: Existing original-plan checker admitted the actual reader, including init, private PID/cgroup namespaces and private 64 MiB /scratch tmpfs.
reader.fault: Fixed contained probe observed the actual child and its inherited lease FD, wrote an old-operation scratch marker, sent SIGSTOP then SIGTERM, and confirmed the child remained stopped/alive. Child pidfd was transferred to a surviving peer before killing only the supervisor through its pidfd.
reader.exit_observation: The external peer's retained original child pidfd became readable after the crash; neither socket EOF nor exec status 137 was used as child-retirement proof. Old child exit code remains unknown.
reader.fresh_root_observation: After Engine restarted this same container and current readiness returned, a contained check observed /scratch empty before the peer opened its successor session.
reader.successor: New generation and operation, same lease identity; no scientific bytes sent; actual successor return code -15 and scratch cleanup confirmed.

scratch_admission_negative: A controlled bind-instead-of-tmpfs inspection mutation was refused by the original-plan checker after the real reader passed. This is file-admission proof, not a bad-container launch.
final_state: Public observe-only up preserved the pending original restriction; public down fenced it and stopped the stack. Six unaffected stopped containers retain bounded Docker logs; the two fenced API IDs were removed after warnings.
limits: No secure-erasure, daemon-restart, scientific accuracy, live-model or external API/GUI claim. Namespace teardown, lease release, fresh scratch and successor admission are separate observations.
